name: Cisco ASA — Internal Port Scan Against Internal Host
xql_query:
datamodel dataset = cisco_asa_raw
| filter cisco_asa_raw._raw_log contains "302014"
| filter xdm.source.interface = "inside" and xdm.target.interface = "inside"
| bin _time span = 10m
| comp count_distinct(xdm.target.port) as distinct_ports,
       values(xdm.target.port) as scanned_ports,
       count() as connection_attempts
       by xdm.target.ipv4, xdm.source.ipv4, _time
| filter distinct_ports >= 100
| alter victim_ip = xdm.target.ipv4, scanner_ip = xdm.source.ipv4
| fields victim_ip, scanner_ip, scanned_ports, distinct_ports, connection_attempts
description: One source IP probing many distinct ports against a single target — internal port scan.
alert_name: Cisco ASA — Internal Port Scan Against Internal Host
alert_description:
What fired: One source IP probing many distinct ports against a single target — internal port scan.

Why it matters: an actor is enumerating hosts, services, shares, or accounts to map the environment. Assessed severity: High.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1046 - Network Service Discovery (TA0007 - Discovery).

Investigate:
  - Identify the scanning source and the number/range of targets it touched.
  - Confirm the source is not an authorized scanner/vuln tool; look for follow-on access to any enumerated target.
  - Pivot on the alert's key entity (xdm.target.ipv4) to related activity in the same window.
  - Confirm the activity is not expected/authorized for the involved entity before escalating.
